cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players struggle with interface scaling and restrictive building limits right away.

claims.claim: UI scaling options cut off important interface elements and menu buttons, requiring external file modifications to adjust settings.

citations.review_text:
UI scaling is absolutely trash. Turning it up to anything past 1.5x causes buttons to get cut off, and the lack of an ability to scroll in most menu places makes it so anything cut off is not accessible until the UI is brought back to normal size. Turning it up to 2x made the options button completely cut off, rendering it impossible to open the settings in the main menu, and requiring it to be changed externally in a file.

People with bad eyesight beware. This game failed to add basic UI scaling in any functional form.

I'll update this review if it gets fixed. If it doesn't though, screw this game. Unplayable for people like me.

I like RTS games, bought because they supported macOS. The interface is obscured and a bug about it is marked "won't fix" because it can be ameliorated by running in windowed mode. It's also still an Intel macOS program, so running under Rosetta. I'm keeping it because they made the effort to publish for macOS, but I can't say I recommend it.

claims.claim: Territory expansion is restricted by strict limits on the number of buildings allowed per zone, requiring players to clear specific criteria and resources to colonize and upgrade land.

citations.review_text:
I feel like i am not the target of this game. I liked settlers 3, and hoped for similar experience.
I will not recommend it because of reasons i consider universal: Its just unpolished.

Pros:
- oldschool gameplay
- Idea of winter and summer - in winter You have less food and people burn wood for heat. Nice idea.
- simple

Cons
- building limits is 3 per tile regardless of the space. Not fun.
- Placing certain building boost production for specific area and one area can only have 3 buildings so You end up doing a tetris to optimize production. Not fun.
- Settlers 3 were more intuitive when it comes to step by step buildings. You did have greyed out ones before You built the basic ones, then You build advanced ones. Here You have most of them at once in second mission.
I do not like the graphics of the zone gradient (which is blue, yellow or green). This could have been done so much better imho.
- Certain buildings can be built only on certain areas. Hunter only on places You have deers, fisherman only in places You have lake and so on. If thats the case it could be equally good to automatically start building of such structures when right after acquiring tile.
- If you build a building you have to manually assign people to this building. Why ? Not fun.
- Peasants automatically start roaming after they are created (born?). Why not make a button to gather all of them if they have nothing to do (like in Age Of Empires) series?

I played only 1.5h and its enough for me.

I'm a fan of Stronghold and AOM so I was hooked by the trailer -- RTS, nordic theme, castle and resource management, a popularity metric, mythical creatures, let's go.

So I got the full game with all the DLCs aaaand... the first mission in the story killed my hype stone dead.

Hey, remember how in those classic games you could just go to a new territory and start building, if there are no enemies around? Well, here you can't, because you need to get a soldier inside a defined "zone" and "colonize" the area -- . Ok, a bit weird that there is bureacracy involved in claiming new lands during the viking age, but never mind. You pay resources to colonize, and after a few minutes the area is yours, let's get building. Oh, you can only assign one villager to build a specific building, so it takes a bit longer but.. wait, why can't I place a hunter's hut in this wide open area?

Because each area you colonize only allows three buildings. Seriously. If you want more, you need to pay more resources to "upgrade the zone." Then, my villagers started starving and the game told me that I can't build any farms or hunters' lodges because "every area that is allowed to have one already has one."

Seriously, this is less AOM and more Zoning Law: The Game. The arbitrary rules and even the vocabulary the game uses are immersion breaking and rob you of the sense of freedom while exploring the wilderness. I might give this another chance but it really fell short of what I was hoping to get.

claims.claim: The game combines traditional real-time strategy mechanics with city-building and survival elements like winter survival and food management.

citations.review_text: Really fun strategy game with a great Viking atmosphere. I like that you have to think not only about fighting, but also about food, resources, territory and surviving the winter. There are quite a few different clans, so you can try different playstyles and find what works best for you. The game is easy to get into, but there’s definitely a lot to learn if you want to get really good at it. I especially enjoyed playing with friends, although the single-player modes are fun too. Overall, a really solid RTS and definitely worth trying if you like strategy games.

Northgard é um RTS bem feito, bonito, com boa trilha sonora, visual mais cartunesco, e mecânicas diferenciadas em relação à suas inspirações (Age Of Empires, Age Of Mythology, ...). Ele acrescenta conceitos de jogos do estilo "city building" (como felicidade, fome, mudanças de estação, ...) ao estilo clássico, o que deixa as partidas mais difíceis e mais longas. Tem uma boa variedade de clãs Vikings, que apresentam algumas características específicas (mas pouca militar, que é expandida com alguns clãs de DLC). Pouca variedade de unidade militares em geral, assim como melhorias, o que pode deixar o jogo desinteressante para que aprecia combates.  Por incrível que pareça as partidas demandam combates constantes com animais e monstros do mapa (sim, o jogo abraça a mitologia), A campanha tem um enredo simples e folclórico, com boa dublagem e que consegue te ensinar um pouco do arroz com feijão (apesar de às vezes os objetivos serem um pouco confusos). As partidas aleatórias contra o computador não são muito personalizáveis: você escolha um tamanho de mapa, seu clã e a dificuldade. A partida tem várias possibilidades de vitória, incluindo economica e militar, mas não é possível escolher somente uma, o que prejudica o foco (na minha experiência). Alguns clãs são desbalanceados, principalmente os de DLC que trazem unidades militares diferenciadas. Em geral eu achei interessante as novas experiências que foram incoporadas neste RTS, apesar das adversidades do clima e mapa sempre estarem te atrasando de uma forma ou de outra, além do desbalanceamento nas partidas aleatórias. Acho que vale conhecer para quem gosta do gênero.

Completei o jogo em um sistema Linux utilizando o SteamPlay (Proton 11.0) sem problemas.
A fun and challenging mix of RTS, civ building and survival.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks in-game explanations or tutorials for core numerical values such as population happiness consumption, food upkeep, wood requirements, and building costs.

citations.review_text: Its a good game, but honestly they need to explain the mechanics of each faction better. they need to add in being able to farm empty plots to many end up with no food and no other resources.

After 35 hours, I can't really recommend this game.  Not as an RTS.

The Pros:
Nice Visuals
Distinct Factions

The Cons
INCREDIBLY Slow Paced
Poor Resource Management System
Lacking Tutorials

Firstly, the promotional videos will lead you to believe this game is action packed.  It's not.  The pacing is incredibly slow. You'll spend most of your time just waiting on things.  There's a LOT of downtime just waiting on resources, which sucks, because 90% of the game is resource management, and the resource management system is incredibly tedious. 

The general system is straight forward.  There's happiness, food, wood, and money.  

Happiness - The higher your happiness, the faster your tribe grows.  Each new member lowers your overall happiness. By how much?  No idea.  The game doesn't tell you. 
Food - Each person requires food.  How much?  No idea.  The game doesn't tell you.  You'll need to set up farms, hunting lodges, or fisheries for food.  How much food do these buildings give?  No idea.  The game doesn't tell you.
Wood - Wood is required to build buildings.  More importantly, it's required to make firewood to heat homes. How much wood do each person need specifically?  No idea.  The game doesn't tell you.
Money - Money is required to purchase and maintain your buildings, to purchase upgrades, and to train military units. How much does it cost to maintain buildings specifically?  No idea.  The game doesn't tell you.

I think you can start to see the problem here.  As a player, you're not really told why your people are starving, or why you're not making enough money.  As a new player, you'll look at your colony and think, "I have a farm, a fishery, and a hunting lodge.  That should be enough food for the rest of the game."  It's not.  You'll constantly be struggling to keep your people fed.  The game goes through seasons, and winter will lower your production of food as well as increase your need for firewood.  By how much, exactly?  No idea.  The game doesn't t…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's pacing as very slow, involving significant downtime spent waiting for resources to accumulate.

citations.review_text:
A friend and I got this many years ago to play as a non-standard kind of RTS. In some ways the game was great fun and in others very frustrating. As the game picked up years and new DLC were released, issues with connectivity were not fixed, balance issues around new clans were constant, and the core mechanic around the game stayed the same, i.e. you need to econ or you will fail.

You could call this game an RTS, but that would be mistaking how slow this game can be and how clans can go without focusing on troops at all. Games can take hours and that only makes the connectivity issues worse when you are trying to play any multiplayer.

I don't dislike the game, but it seems to be lacking the love it needs to not be chore to play at times. A frustrating game stops being enjoyable, which is why my friend and I have stopped playing and why I would not recommend this game to others.

Skip Northgard.


I waited nine years to finally play Northgard, because I cannot ethically support a game until it is complete. The devs kept churning out new useless DLC for many years. I did buy what I thought was the final DLC ages ago when the devs said no more, only for them to release even more. The biggest flaw in Northgard for me is that the devs had nine years to add more story, and instead all that I have is two rather short campaigns alongside of a mountain of cash-grab DLC which adds no story whatsoever, plus some game modes to be played once due to not seeing any real replay value from the samey gameplay loop. I have like 10 times the amount of time put into Starcraft 2 for its story alone, because the story was actually important to those devs.

Flaws:
-This entire game is mostly waiting, sitting alt-tabbed while the game plays by itself because it is just sooo slooow.

-Scouts should not hurt while generating favour with other clans, and if playing politics, then they should not be listed as being hurt while “exploring another zone.” I can send scouts to other town halls to generate favour, but AI never does that to me, to generate favour with me. Where is allied victory, after befriending everyone? Why give us a diplomacy tab but no means to be diplomatic and ally mid-game or win together when not starting as allies? 100% relations, still get attacked by supposed friend. Diplomacy is overall useless and unfinished other than allowing you to get one giant unit once from a giant faction if first to 100%.

-Almost every single map is an island, a noticeable design choice which I do not care for, thematically. I get that there are (paid DLC) water-centric clans and they need to not be completely useless (to sell the DLC), but other water-clan gimmicks in similar games have figured out how to do this other than make every map an island.

-Across all modes, only combat wins feel worthwhile. All of the other win conditions are just “wait for ba…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface as cluttered with pop-up notices that interrupt gameplay during battles.

citations.review_text: Extremely show gameplay and to much popup during combat.

Game is bugged so that healers frequently are not healing.

The game controls fight you - the game wont allow you to select units from too far to the side of the screen, by default it pops up with notices that you have to click out of in the middle of battle, units feel unresponsive after playing other RTSs.

The game revolves around team games withg resouces randomly generated. This has 2 issues: you frequently get attacked by different factions in multiple places and you cannot win without your whole army in one place (since army efficieny also scales with unit count). If you spawn with bad resources around you you're screwed from the start.

Ladder is pretty dead, especially for "new" players.

I tried really hard to like this game as I have a freind who liked it, but I just cant recommend it to others

Northgard is an interesting concept on an RTS game consisting of nothing but vikings.

You would imagine it would have a stronger focus on combat but that doesn't really seem to be the case alot of the time.  Making sure you have a strong economy, keeping track of the seasons, and watching your opponents and what their goals are.  These are the things that come into play when you play this game, and it really nails down just how unforgiving things can be if you aren't on top of your people's development.

I've played a fair share of RTS games and the campaign does a great job of teaching you what's what.  I'm not going to defend the story as it's pretty basic but, honestly, it made a solid effort and I can respect that.  The UI can be somewhat "involved" so it may take abit of time to get a grasp on where to look at this and that but it's really not too bad.

All in all, solid as hell game.  8/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that new DLC clans suffer from power creep and make balance issues worse.

citations.review_text: good with friends. some dlc clans are OP though

I have over 900 hours in Northgard, so this isn't a review from someone who just lost a few matches. I've played this game for years because I genuinely enjoyed it, but the current state of the game is incredibly disappointing.

The clan balance is a complete mess. Instead of properly balancing existing clans, it feels like every new DLC clan is released overtuned just to drive sales. Then it takes forever to address the obvious issues, if they get addressed at all.

On top of that, my recent multiplayer games have been filled with cheaters. Whether it's map hacks or other exploits, it's becoming more and more common, and it feels like there is little to no moderation.

The biggest problem is that it honestly seems like none of the developers actually play their own game at a high level. Many balance changes make no sense from a competitive perspective, and obvious issues remain untouched for months.

It's frustrating because Northgard has an amazing foundation, but right now it feels like it's being managed without understanding what makes the game enjoyable or fair.

I can't recommend it in its current state.

I still find this game really fun and engaging in PVP and Conquest. Love some of the new clans and their flexibility/new mechanics.
The only issue I can see with it is power creep with DLC clans and older beloved clans falling behind or being nerfed into the ground because of the newer clans (Raven, Bear, Ox, Stag)

Winning!! 

At the moment the game is Brutal BS above Normal.
good with friends. some dlc clans are OP though

claims.claim: Reviewers report that healers do not heal and the Bifrost game mode fails to give rewards.

citations.review_text:
Game is bugged so that healers frequently are not healing.

The game controls fight you - the game wont allow you to select units from too far to the side of the screen, by default it pops up with notices that you have to click out of in the middle of battle, units feel unresponsive after playing other RTSs.

The game revolves around team games withg resouces randomly generated. This has 2 issues: you frequently get attacked by different factions in multiple places and you cannot win without your whole army in one place (since army efficieny also scales with unit count). If you spawn with bad resources around you you're screwed from the start.

Ladder is pretty dead, especially for "new" players.

I tried really hard to like this game as I have a freind who liked it, but I just cant recommend it to others
The Bifrost game mode doesn't give rewards. This is a known bug that has been present and prominent for more than a year, and the devs have not fixed it yet. Superb game, but it feels abandoned.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience server instability, lag, and connection drops during multiplayer sessions.

citations.review_text: I think the game is pretty cool, but i'm very dissapointed with the bad servers in which I play in. I play other games such as age of empires without any issue, but with this game my units don't move for half of a round. It's very frustrating and it needs to be improved.

i played this game for too long, ugly bad devs but beautiful game im sad to see it go down this way.
single player is fine, conquest is fine, bifrost is fine.
meanwhile multiplayer is so doomed that i cant even explain how bad it is (servers lag, game crashes, people cant log in, match making is worst than league of legends).
all that money they made just to add freaky games that will fail due to similar problems as the original game absolutely insanity how many dumb decisions one can make, i hope a new game with similar design gets created so i can see shiro falls to the lowest pits along side their broken game and multiplayer, i hope for its downfall more than riot games it self which says a lot.

DO NOT BUY UNLESS FOR SINGLE PLAYER MODES

They're abandoning the game in a fundamentally broken state to focus on mobile-port tier garbage. Unplayable single player since the AI just . . . doesn't work on any difficulty. Unplayable multiplayer since the servers are still massively unstable and will disconnect on a regular basis. Not to even mention the fact that the meta is stale af since multiplayer and singleplayer balance are fundamentally different and Shiro has never addressed this.

Oh, and there are multiple game-breaking bugs that still haven't been addressed, including the new clan being actually unplayable in conquest since their VERY FIRST mission that is always the same is bugged. The map does not generate correctly, making the objective unachievable.
Just avoid this studio at all costs. The moment the effort to develop a game outweighs the money coming in from it, they will jump ship and spit in the faces of everyone who has supported them.
